name: Isolated Lower Lip Fistula

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Isolated Lower Lip Fistula

criteria.description: Presence of a congenital fistulous tract on the lower lip without associated syndromic features
Radiologic or fistulography confirmation of a fistulous tract originating from the lower lip
Absence of other craniofacial anomalies or syndromic associations such as Van der Woude syndrome
Histopathological confirmation of fistula lined by squamous epithelium

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital lower lip fistula confirmed clinically and radiologically with exclusion of syndromic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing may be considered to exclude syndromic causes.

pathognomonic.notes: Visible or palpable fistulous tract on the vermilion border of the lower lip
searchTerms: small hole on lower lip present from birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent mucous or serous discharge from lower lip fistula
pathognomonic.notes: Intermittent drainage without signs of infection
searchTerms: repeated mucus or clear fluid from lip opening

common.symptomName: Lower lip swelling adjacent to fistula
common.notes: Mild localized swelling due to fistula tract
searchTerms: lip area swelling adjacent to fistula

common.symptomName: Intermittent discomfort or tenderness at fistula site
Difficulty with lip seal or mild drooling
common.notes: Due to fistula tract affecting lip integrity

occasional.symptomName: Secondary bacterial infection of fistula tract
occasional.notes: May cause pain, swelling, and purulent discharge

occasional.symptomName: Cosmetic concerns related to fistula appearance
occasional.notes: May affect self-esteem in older children or adults

rare.notes: Mild underdevelopment of lower lip tissue

rare.symptomName: Fistula tract extending into underlying musculature

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests unless secondary infection present
Microbiological culture of fistula discharge if infected
imaging: Fistulography demonstrating fistulous tract from lower lip to subcutaneous tissues
Ultrasound or MRI to delineate tract anatomy
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified in isolated cases
Genetic testing to exclude syndromic causes such as IRF6 mutations in Van der Woude syndrome
other: Histopathology showing fistula lined by stratified squamous epithelium
Clinical exclusion of associated craniofacial anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of lower lip pits often bilateral
Positive family history and IRF6 gene mutation
Absence of discharge or intermittent plugging
Acute onset with pain, swelling, erythema

redFlags: Rapidly increasing swelling or pain suggesting abscess formation
Signs of systemic infection such as fever or malaise
Presence of additional craniofacial anomalies indicating syndromic involvement
references: Orphanet: Isolated Lower Lip Fistula - ORPHA:141064
Smith et al. (2018). Congenital lower lip fistulas: Clinical features and management. Journal of Craniofacial Surgery.
Jones and Patel (2020). Differential diagnosis of congenital lower lip anomalies. Pediatric Otolaryngology.
